newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps weaken with Iraq news, bar fuel.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps weaken with Iraq news, bar fuel.

text.p: European oil swaps rallied in the morning then reversed gains in the afternoon after bearish news from Iraq hit the market. Only fuel was resistant to the drop.
The United Nations said talks had been finalised on a food distribution plan, the stumbling block to renewed exports which have been halted since the end of May.

Brent CFDs lost a cent or so in prompt contracts, but were broadly steady further out compared with Friday. July 14-18 was pegged at -17/18 cents against September Brent from -17 cents with July 21-25 at -22/23 from -24 cents. July 28-August 1 was talked steady around -25/26 cents against September while August 4-8 was assessed unchanged at -26/27 cents.

Before screen crude headed southwards July 10-18 was sold at -10 cents against August and again at -13 cents against September. After crude's slide a July 21-25 July 28-August 1 roll went at 3.5 cents and July 21-25 went at -24 against September. July 28 to August 1 went at -26 cents against September.
Gasoline saw an August swap trade at $188 in the morning, but in the afternoon levels were down to $184-186. July was talked early at $187, but had fallen to $184 by the end of the day.

Naphtha had a mini run higher before getting knocked lower by crude. Some physical support was given in the guise of refinery demand for N+A and strong Asian prices. August was pegged around $181-182 having earlier toyed with $183-184 while September was about $1 backwardated.

Heavy fuel was the most resistant product with swaps steady to a touch firmer, albeit in a slow market. July was valued around $86-86.50 with August marginally firmer. An August cif cargo swap was done at $85.50 and a September barge went at $87.50. 4Q was talked around $92.50 and 1Q around $96.00.
